description: Your Lord Has Not Forsaken You by Najwa Awad and Sarah Sultan, both experienced Muslim counsellors, is a guide to understanding trauma and its far-reaching effects on the body, mind and soul. Trauma is more common than many realise and can quietly drain our energy, happiness and even our faith for years. The authors explain how it can lead to cognitive biases and doubts around faith, and how to grow beyond these roadblocks and find contentment. At its heart is the al-Duha Approach: how Allah comforted the Prophet ﷺ through Surah ad-Duha, and how the surah offers a framework for Islamic psychology today. The book also includes a library of clinically proven coping skills and real-life case studies, and is warmly recommended by Omar Suleiman of Yaqeen Institute. Allah says, “Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested you” (Quran 93:3). title: I Became a Muslim
description: I Became a Muslim is Aysha Parry’s honest memoir of her path from a Christian upbringing in England to Islam. She describes her growing disillusionment, a spiritual search that took her around the world, and how the call to prayer moved her as nothing else had, before she built a new life in Egypt. Parry writes openly about the challenges she faced both before and after her conversion. It suits anyone considering Islam, new Muslims, and readers who want to understand the convert’s experience from the inside. Allah says, “So whoever Allah wants to guide – He expands his breast to [contain] Islam” (Quran 6:125). title: Traversing the Highs and Lows of Muslim Marriage

It speaks to those preparing for marriage, newlyweds adjusting to daily life together and long-married couples whose relationship is under strain. The author tackles real challenges such as the behaviour of in-laws, a spouse’s conduct and threats to a couple’s privacy, while questioning cultural norms and stereotypes that can hold marriages back. Her advice shows how to build a strong, lasting bond and resolve problems constructively. Allah says, “And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy” (Quran 30:21). He argues that men and women are equal in respect but different in role, and that the problems facing Muslim women stem from the gap between Islamic principles and actual practice. He also notes that Western civilisation developed its guiding principles apart from religion. Reasoned and thought-provoking, it suits readers interested in comparative study and in understanding the Islamic perspective on women. Allah says, “Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life” (Quran 16:97). Key Features Author: Maulana Wahiduddin Khan Publisher: Goodword Books Format: Paperback, 252 pages Language: English Approach: Comparative study

It explains why the rows matter, how the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions straightened them, and the common mistakes to avoid. A helpful read for imams, masjid committees, students and every worshipper who prays in congregation. The Prophet ﷺ said, “Straighten your rows, for straightening the rows is part of establishing the prayer” (Sahih al-Bukhari). title: The Sunnah and Its Role in Islamic Legislation
description: Dr Mustafa as-Siba’ee’s scholarly study explains the status of the Sunnah as a source of Islamic law and traces its history from the beginning of revelation to its recording by the great hadith imams. It also sets out how scholars preserved the Sunnah, sifted out fabrications and developed the hadith sciences. The book summarises and answers the critics of the Sunnah, past and present, including those raised historically and by modern Orientalists. Long studied by Arabic-speaking students, it is valuable for students of Islamic studies and serious readers. Allah says, “And whatever the Messenger has given you – take; and what he has forbidden you – refrain from” (Quran 59:7). Key Features Author: Dr Mustafa as-Siba’ee Translator: Faisal Muhammad Shafeeq Publisher: IIPH Language: English Format: Hardback, 570 pages

The book shows how Eid is celebrated with family, friends and the wider community. They visit the mosque, meet friends and enjoy delicious food and carnival rides, while their parents explain the true meaning of Eid-ul-Fitr. Colourful illustrations make it an engaging read for children in the lead-up to Eid. Allah says, “…and to glorify Allah for that to which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful” (Quran 2:185). Key Features Publisher: Goodword Series: I’m Learning About Subject: The meaning of Eid-ul-Fitr Covers: Eid prayer and charity Illustrations: Colourful

title: The Correct Islamic Aqidah & That Which Opposes It
description: In The Correct Islamic Aqidah and That Which Opposes It, Shaykh Abdul-Aziz ibn Baz explains that sound belief is the foundation of Islam. It shows that deeds and words are only accepted when they arise from correct belief, then sets out the six pillars of faith: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and divine decree, both its good and its bad. He also clarifies the beliefs and practices that contradict these pillars, so that the reader can protect their faith. Concise and clearly written, it is an ideal starting point for new Muslims, young people, students of knowledge and study circles. Allah says, “Say, ‘He is Allah, [who is] One’” (Quran 112:1). Simple text and beautiful colour illustrations capture young readers’ interest, making the box a lovely choice for reading together at home, in the classroom or as an Eid gift. Read the books aloud with younger children or let early readers enjoy them on their own. Allah says, “We relate to you the best of stories” (Quran 12:3). title: Ard Al Zaafaran Al Dur Al Makhoon Air Freshener 300ml
description: Ard Al Zaafaran Al Dur Al Makhoon Air Freshener 300ml is an air freshener spray with a fruity, leathery scent. It is ideal for bedrooms, living areas, offices, prayer spaces and guest rooms. Spray into the air as needed, away from your face and polished surfaces, for a quick refresh before guests arrive, after cooking or before prayer. A practical everyday companion to bakhoor and oud when you want fragrance without lighting a burner. Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ would never refuse a gift of perfume (Sahih al-Bukhari). description: A Gift to my Brothers by Shaykh Mufti Saiful Islam is a collection of short, thought-provoking articles written to encourage fathers, brothers, husbands and sons towards an Islamic way of life. It includes real-life stories of the pious predecessors, illustrations, and practical advice, including on intoxicants and rehabilitation. Easy to dip into, it makes a good companion for personal reading and a thoughtful gift for the men in your family. Shaykh Mufti Saiful Islam is the founder of Jamiah Khatamun Nabiyeen (JKN) in Bradford, UK, and editor of the family magazine Al-Mu'min. description: The Al-Harameen HA-5115 is a large mosque-style Azan wall clock with a bright LED display of all prayer times and the date. It plays the complete Azan for all five daily prayers with adjustable volume, and prayer alarms adjust automatically as prayer times change. Prayer times are available for major cities worldwide, with Hijri and Gregorian dates, 12 or 24-hour time and an automatic daylight-saving option, and it is available in gold or silver. It suits masjids, prayer rooms and larger homes. Allah says, “Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times” (Quran 4:103). description: The Miraculous Baby by Saniyasnain Khan is a beautifully illustrated, creatively written title in Goodword’s Quran Stories for Little Hearts series. It tells the story of the life of Prophet Isa (AS) as portrayed in the Quran, retold in gentle, simple language for young children. Its gentle tone makes it a lovely first introduction to one of the great prophets of Islam. Simple text and colourful illustrations hold the attention of little readers, making it a lovely choice for reading together at home or in the classroom. Allah says, “He said, ‘Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet’” (Quran 19:30). title: Family Interactions – Successful Family Upbringing 3
description: Family Interactions is Book 3 of the Successful Family Upbringing series by Prof. Dr Abdul Karim Bakkar. It examines how family members relate to one another, setting out the key concepts and methods for improving communication and building strong relationships at home. Drawing on Islamic teaching and psychology, the author offers practical ways to handle disagreements, strengthen emotional bonds and foster mutual respect. Ideal for parents, guardians and older children who want a calmer, more harmonious home. The Prophet ﷺ said, “Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock” (Sahih al-Bukhari). description: A Gift to the Husband and Wife brings together excerpts from the writings of Maulana Ashraf Ali Thanvi on marriage. It covers the relationship between spouses after marriage, their mutual rights, and the common problems that lead to marital breakdown, along with their causes. Drawing on verses of the Quran, the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ and real-life examples, it guides both newly married and experienced couples towards a peaceful home. It also makes a meaningful wedding gift. Allah says, “And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy” (Quran 30:21). description: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: The Messenger of Allah is a beautifully illustrated board book by Saniyasnain Khan that introduces children to the life and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
